To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the ectopic ascitic antigen of 91kDa-molecular weight, which is sharing antigenicity with a calcium-binding protein MRP8 and a 28kDa-protein of the human placenta, is recognized to be expressed in mesenchyme- and myeloid-derived cells such as placental macrophages (or Hofbauer cells), foetal monocytes, endothelial cells, fibroblasts etc. in the first and early second trimesters of gestation.

the 91kDA-ectopic protein was detected in the human placental tissue macroages (Hofbauers cells), foetal myeloid lineagse, fibroblasts and endothelial cells, but not in the cytotrophobasts, in the first and the second trimesters of gestation, as revealed by the immunoelectron microscopic colloidal-gold technique.
the 91kD-protein, an ectopic ascitic protein, was found in myeloid lineaged cells and/or mesenchyme-derived tissues in the human placental tissue at the first and second stages of pregnancy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cellular localization and the dynamics of 91kDa protein in the human placental tissues by the electron microscopic immunocolloid-gold technique.

the cellular characterization of ectopic ascitic protein sharing antigenicity with 28kDa- and MRP8/Cramp, and the possible roles of calcium-binding proteins in the human placental barrier and differentiation of foetal cells.
a new approach for the study of placental physiology, and may be applicable to the study of other organs
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the 91kda-protein is an ectopically expressed oncodevelopmental protein that is shared antigenicity with MPR8/CFA and, thus, is involved in the differentiation of myeloid cell lineages and/or placental barrier functions.

the antigenic epitopes of the 91-kDa-ectopic protein and MRP8 are expressed in the myeloid lineagessuch as placental tissue-derived macrophages and fibroblasts and/or myelomonocytoid cells including endothelial and epithelial cells in the first and early-second trimesters of gestation, but not in the cytotrophoblastic cells.
91kDa protein is a member of the S-100 family and that it is involved in the regulation of cell proliferation, differentiation and/or cell-cell interaction in the human placental tissues.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the placenta is an important source of 91kDa protein, and that the placenta may play a role in the pathophysiological mechanisms of tumour-related dynamics and pregnancy-associated changes.
the 91kda-protein is one of the ectopic proteins that is produced by myeloid lineagous cells and, then, incorporated into the syncytioblast of the placenta.
the antigenic appearances of the 91- and 28-kDa-proteins are closely related to the cell differentiation of the human placenta.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 91kDA ectopic protein is a calcium binding protein that is expressed in the human placental mesenchyme and foetal myeloid cells.
the 91kD-protein is a placental-specific protein, and that the antigenic appearance in the placenta is dependent on the stage of pregnancy.
91kDa ectopic ascitic protein is a placental calcium-binding protein that is present in the syncyotrophoblast.
